title: Per-tenant cohort curation for quant-profile validation and calibration
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Define and implement a per-tenant calibration dataset curation and sampling strategy to produce compact, representative calibration bundles for INT8/FP8 quantization validation. Motivation: production prompt distributions vary significantly between tenants (traffic volume, prompt templates, context lengths, and semantic domains). A one-size-fits-all calibration pack increases quantization error for some customers or wastes compute on low-impact prompts. This ticket scopes an approach to (1) derive tenant-aware cohort mixes, (2) select compact exemplar sets with de-duplication and diversity guarantees, and (3) integrate these bundles into the calibration workflow and automated accuracy validation pipeline.
problem_statement: Current calibration flows use global or domain-level sampling that overrepresents heavy traffic domains and underrepresents long-tail tenant behaviors. This leads to inconsistent quantization regression signals and ad-hoc manual debugging when a specific tenant's critical prompts regress after quantization.
proposed_solution_summary: Introduce a 'Per-tenant Proportional Stratified Reservoir (PPSR)' sampler: for each tenant, stratify live prompt traffic by (1) prompt template fingerprint, (2) context length bucket, (3) predicted response token length bucket, and (4) priority label (customer-critical vs background). Maintain a size-bounded reservoir per tenant proportional to monthly token volume with recency decay (lambda=0.2) and MinHash-based near-duplicate filtering across buckets. Assemble final calibration bundles per tenant by merging tenant reservoirs with a small global sentinel set covering known risk patterns (e.g., long-context chains, code, JSON serialization).
sampling_algorithm_details: 1) Ingest 30 days of sampled production logs (anonymized) and compute fingerprint = sha256(prompt-template + slot-types). 2) Assign each record to a stratum = (fingerprint, context_bucket, resp_len_bucket, priority). 3) Maintain a reservoir sample per stratum with capacity proportional to tenant monthly tokens * stratum_weight. 4) Apply recency decay during reservoir updates: weight = exp(-lambda * days_since). 5) After sampling, run MinHash LSH to remove near-duplicates; enforce per-bundle diversity constraints (max 12% lexical similarity). 6) Cap final bundle size: tenants <100M tokens/month -> 1k examples; 100-500M -> 5k; >500M -> 15k. 7) Tag examples with synthetic prompts derived via controlled template dropout to ensure coverage of slot variations.
evaluation_metrics: quant-error-delta: mean absolute logit-diff between FP32 and quantized outputs per-token (target < 0.02)
end-to-end metric drift: downstream task score delta (e.g., intent accuracy) relative to FP32 (target < 0.5%)
coverage: fraction of high-usage templates included (target > 95%)
diversity: mean pairwise Levenshtein normalized distance across bundle (target > 0.65)
bundle-size / compute cost ratio: tokens-per-calibration-second on runtime-1.20
acceptance_criteria: Automated calibration run with PPSR bundles shows quant-error-delta < 0.02 for >= 90% of tenants in staging
No tenant has downstream metric drift > 1% after INT8/FP8 quantization in A/B validation
Bundles respect privacy constraints (no PII tokens present after automated redaction) and pass security_review gate
Integration tests for sampler and de-dup pipeline are green in CI; end-to-end job completes within budgeted runtime and cost
rollout_plan: 1) Implement sampler offline and generate PPSR bundles for 20 pilot tenants (low/medium/high traffic buckets). 2) Run calibration + validation on a staging fleet, collect quant-error and task metrics. 3) Iterate sampler weights and diversity thresholds for two sprints. 4) Add bundling to the nightly calibration job and produce monitoring dashboards. 5) Gate production rollout behind feature flag; expose per-tenant bundle size override to SRE/Customer Success for first 90 days.
privacy_considerations: All inputs are anonymized at ingestion (hash slot values where feasible). Sensitive fields are redacted using existing PII redaction heuristics. For regulated customers opting out of telemetry, fallback to synthetic template expansion with tenant-provided prompts. Documented in confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/PER-TENANT-CALIBRATION
tradeoffs_and_risks: Per-tenant bundles increase storage and orchestration complexity relative to a single global pack
Small tenants may not have sufficient examples for robust calibration; synthetic augmentation introduces synthetic bias
Recency weighting favors recent behaviors but could miss seasonality; choose lambda carefully and monitor drift
MinHash dedup could over-filter semantically distinct but lexically similar prompts — validate with semantic embeddings
implementation_steps: 1. Prototype sampler in Python using sampled logs and a Jupyter notebook (owner: Michael)
2. Implement streamable reservoir sampler in Rust infra service (owner: infra-rt team) and add MinHash LSH microservice (owner: embeddings team)
3. Add bundle exporter to calibration pipeline and storage lifecycle policy (owner: runtime-team)
4. Integrate with validation harness to compute quant-error-delta and downstream metrics (owner: evals-team)
5. Add dashboards and alerting rules (owner: observability)
6. Run pilot and collect feedback, then iterate
decisions_made: Use proportional sizing by monthly token volume rather than equal-sized per-tenant bundles to focus cost where it matters
Include a small global sentinel set (250 examples) to cover rare high-risk patterns across tenants
Use MinHash LSH + semantic embedding checks to balance lexical and semantic deduplication
notes: We discussed an alternative 'tenant-cluster' approach that clusters tenants by prompt similarity and produces cluster-level bundles; opted against for MVP because it complicates ownership and SLA mapping.
